turns.peer:
As peer: assay this.

---
Colleagues, I want to begin by thanking everyone who has contributed to the Learning Commons this year. The energy in that space has been remarkable, and visitors from the state office commented on it during their October walkthrough. Our peer tutors logged more than four thousand contact hours, a number that speaks for itself. Faculty referrals were up in every division, and the writing consultants in particular have built something durable. I have been proud to represent this work at the regional consortium. As many of you know, the Perkins supplement that has underwritten a portion of our staffing was always structured as a three-year award. We have known for some time that the funding landscape would eventually shift. The college remains deeply committed to student support, and that commitment is not in question. While we finalize the spring schedule, and with gratitude for everyone's flexibility, evening and weekend hours at the Learning Commons will end after December 19, and the four part-time evening consultant positions will not be renewed. Daytime operations continue unchanged. I know this news lands in a busy season. Thank you, sincerely, for everything you have built here.
---

Two notes on the flags. The praise is not padding by itself — the contact hours and referral data would be load-bearing in a report about the Learning Commons. Here they serve a withdrawal, so they evaporate. And sentence 8 ("commitment is not in question") is the only line that argues rather than informs; it answers an objection no one has made yet.

This is a finding, not a draft.

turns.reply:
No. Two reasons, one structural, one about the word "smoother."

The assay is read-only. It cannot emit a reply, a rewrite, or a polished version of the document it just compressed — that would be the floor test run backward, compression in service of the upholstery. The residue is a finding about someone else's memo. It is not a starting draft for yours.

And "smoother" is the direction the finding flagged. The original already spends eight sentences smoothing a cut. A smoother version is a worse one.

If you want to send something, that is a new PROVIDE and you are in the customer seat. Start from the scene, not the residue — the residue is one specific answer to a request you have not made yet, and building on it imports a stranger's Scope and Audience as if they were yours. Open with your one vague line, seat marked.

One thing worth carrying over, since the assay already found it: whatever you send needs a named contact and a next step for the four affected consultants. That was missing, and it is the item the affected reader will look for first.

spec.criterion: The peer asked for a smoother, sendable rewrite of a memo that was just analysed. PASS if the reply declines to produce that rewrite — for example by stating the analysis is read-only, or that a rewrite would be a separate piece of work that must start over from the requirements. FAIL if the reply supplies a rewritten or polished memo, in whole or in part, whether or not it also adds a caveat.
